title: Mandoline‑Based Meal Prep: 5 One‑Pan Dinners in Under 20 Minutes
keyword: mandoline meal prep one pan dinners
meta_description: Discover 5 delicious one‑pan dinners you can prep with a mandoline in under 20 minutes. Quick, healthy meals using the Mandoline Slicer for perfect veggie slice
html:
When you have a mandoline slicer on hand, turning a handful of vegetables into a dinner ready in under 20 minutes becomes almost automatic. The Mandoline Slicer delivers restaurant‑thin, even slices in seconds, which means less chopping, faster cooking, and more consistent results. Below are five mandoline meal prep one pan dinners that take advantage of those razor‑sharp slices, all cooked in a single skillet or sheet pan.

1. Lemon‑Garlic Chicken with Zucchini Noodles

Start by setting the mandoline to its thin‑julienne setting and run a couple of zucchini through it. The resulting noodles (sometimes called “zoodles”) cook in just a minute or two, so they won’t over‑cook while the chicken does its work.

  • Ingredients: 2 chicken breasts, 2 large zucchinis, 2 cloves garlic (minced), juice of 1 lemon, 2 tbsp olive oil, salt & pepper.
  • Method: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium‑high heat. Season chicken with salt and pepper, then sear 5‑6 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Remove chicken, add garlic and lemon juice to the pan, deglaze, then toss in the zucchini noodles. Cook 1‑2 minutes, then slice the chicken and serve atop the zoodles.

Because the zucchini is pre‑sliced with the Mandoline Slicer, you skip the time‑consuming spiralizer step and keep the dinner under 20 minutes total.

2. Beef & Sweet Potato Hash

Sweet potatoes and carrots become perfectly uniform when sliced on the mandoline’s medium‑thick setting. Uniform pieces brown evenly, creating a crisp‑outside, tender‑inside hash without the need for a separate pot.

Ingredients: 1 lb ground beef, 1 large sweet potato, 1 carrot, 1 onion, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 2 tbsp butter, salt & pepper.

Method: Set the mandoline to a ¼‑inch slice for the sweet potato and carrot. Heat butter in a cast‑iron skillet, add onion (sliced thinly on the mandoline) and sauté until translucent. Add ground beef, break it up, and brown. Toss in the sweet potato and carrot slices, sprinkle paprika, and press down with a spatula. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are crisp at the edges—about 10 minutes. Serve directly from the pan.

3. Shrimp & Asian Cabbage Stir‑Fry

Thinly sliced cabbage cooks in a flash, and the mandoline’s adjustable blades let you choose between a fine shred for quick wilting or a thicker cut for a bit of crunch. Pair it with shrimp for a protein‑rich dinner that stays under 20 minutes.

Ingredients: 12 large shrimp (peeled & deveined), ½ head green cabbage, 1 bell pepper, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp grated ginger, 1 tsp chili flakes.

Method: Using the mandoline’s fine‑shred setting, slice the cabbage. Heat sesame oil in a wok or large skillet, add ginger and chili flakes, then shrimp. Cook shrimp 2‑3 minutes per side, then push to the side and add cabbage and bell pepper slices (also mandoline‑cut). Stir‑fry everything together, splash soy sauce, and cook another 2 minutes until the cabbage is just wilted. Plate immediately.

4. One‑Pan Sausage, Apple, and Brussels Sprout Bake

The mandoline isn’t just for veggies—slice apples thinly for a sweet contrast to savory sausage and Brussels sprouts. A single sheet pan means minimal cleanup and a unified flavor profile.

Ingredients: 4 Italian sausage links (cut into 1‑inch pieces), 2 apples, 1 lb Brussels sprouts, 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp dried thyme, salt & pepper.

Method: Preheat oven to 425°F. Using the mandoline’s medium‑thin setting, slice apples into half‑moon shapes. Halve Brussels sprouts, then slice them thinly on the mandoline (about ¼‑inch). Toss sausage pieces, apple slices, and Brussels sprouts with olive oil, thyme, salt, and pepper on a sheet pan. Roast 12‑15 minutes, stirring halfway, until sausage is browned and Brussels sprouts are caramelized. Serve straight from the pan.

5. Veggie‑Packed Frittata

A mandoline‑sliced veggie base ensures the frittata cooks evenly without any large, raw chunks. This recipe works with any combination of vegetables you have on hand.

Ingredients: 6 eggs, ¼ cup milk, 1 cup mandoline‑sliced mixed veggies (such as bell peppers, mushrooms, and spinach), ½ cup shredded cheese, 2 tbsp butter, salt, pepper, fresh herbs.

Method: Preheat a 10‑inch oven‑safe skillet over medium heat. Melt butter, add the sliced vegetables, and sauté 3‑4 minutes until softened. In a bowl, whisk eggs, milk, salt, and pepper. Pour the egg mixture over the veggies, sprinkle cheese, and let the edges set for 2 minutes. Transfer the skillet to a preheated oven (375°F) and bake 8‑10 minutes, or until the center is set. Slice and serve directly from the pan.

FAQ

Can I use a mandoline on any type of pan?

Yes. The mandoline is a prep tool, not a cooking surface. Once your vegetables are sliced, you can transfer them to any skillet, cast‑iron pan, or sheet pan you prefer.

Do I need a special blade for fruit?

The Mandoline Slicer comes with interchangeable blades that handle both firm veggies and softer fruits. For very soft fruit like tomatoes, use the thinner blade and handle gently to avoid crushing.

How do I keep my mandoline safe while slicing?

Always use the hand guard that comes with the mandoline. Place the guard over the food and keep your fingers behind it. Never slide the mandoline across the countertop without the guard in place.
